rulings.raw: 2 ½ pounds stew meat (cut into 1-inch cubes)
rulings.evidence: The main protein: no commodity claims it but today's captures carry matching products, so a null here would pantry-price 2.5 lb of beef. Proposed as a new id through the registrar; boneless chuck cubed for stew is its own fresh-case cut and price class, not ground beef and not a roast.

The board's 'garlic' match is fresh bulb garlic - a different food, price class and gram weight, exactly the 2026-08-26 garlic-powder precedent. Garlic salt is a pantry blend at 1 tsp; pantry-static pricing is safe.
Exact same-form vocabulary row All-Purpose Flour [flour]; board carries flour 7 of 7.
'Cold' is a temperature instruction, not a form: same product as Butter [butter], which the board carries 7 of 7 and the DB already has a row for.
Same-form row Dry White Wine [white-wine], board 4 of 7. Deliberately NOT white-wine-vinegar - that is the wrong dinner and the standing form-flip rejection.
Button mushroom is the retail name for the white mushroom; same product, same price class, board 7 of 7. Portobello is a different, dearer product.
Exact same-form vocabulary row Yellow Onion [onions]; board 7 of 7. Small onion weighed at 70 g.

rulings.raw: 1 tsp better than bouillon (or 1 beef bouillon cube)
rulings.evidence: The line itself names a bouillon cube as the equal alternative, so the concentrated-bouillon concept is what the recipe buys; board carries bouillon 6 of 7. Flagging that I could not verify the board id's flavour is beef rather than chicken.
Tap water for the cornstarch slurry: nothing is bought and it contributes no macros. Kept on the line list so the method still reads.

rulings.raw: 10.5 oz. condensed cream of mushroom soup (optional)
rulings.evidence: Same-form vocabulary row Cream of Mushroom Soup [cream-of-mushroom-soup]; condensed IS the canned form of that product. The board match shown ('mushrooms') is a fuzzy miss and I ignored it. Line is marked optional by the source.
Same-form vocabulary row Egg Noodles [egg-noodles]; 'wide homestyle' is a cut of the same dry product. The board match shown ('eggs') is a fuzzy miss and would price the wrong food.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: No commodity in any namespace claims it per the pre-resolve table, yet today's captures carry matching products, so it is stocked and priceable. The food is boneless beef chuck cut into 1-inch cubes, sold in the fresh beef case per lb: not ground-beef (different cut, different price), not a whole chuck roast (sold uncut, cheaper per lb), not a steak id. If the estate already prices this under a spelling like 'stew-beef' or 'beef-chuck-stew', alias it there rather than minting.
